extracted.intended_audience: Mathematicians, math educators, and enthusiasts preparing submissions (articles, problems, proofs, reviews, puzzles) for Mathematics Magazine (MAA).
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting expository mathematics content (articles, problems & solutions, proofs without words, reviews, puzzles) to Mathematics Magazine, aimed at a broad mathematical audience including strong undergraduates and collegiate teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience and appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishes expository articles meant to appeal to a broad mathematical audience that includes strong undergraduate students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should assume minimal background knowledge and aim to make their work accessible to a broad audience, including well-prepared undergraduates; the magazine primarily targets teachers of collegiate mathematics and their students, offering stimulating supplements for undergraduate courses and fresh perspectives on mathematical history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope / accepted content types
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics Magazine publishes high-quality, original expository research, historical material, interdisciplinary connections, and creative submissions (e.g., logic puzzles, crossword puzzles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted article types listed explicitly: Articles, Problems and Solutions, Proofs Without Words, Reviews, Logic puzzles. Ensure submission fits one of these types and the Magazine's expository mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository clarity and engagement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor an informal and expressive writing style with an active voice. Exposition should be accessible, engaging, and pedagogically useful to the target readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumed background and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write so that well-prepared undergraduates and collegiate instructors can follow; avoid unnecessary technical prerequisites and explain essential context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions must be prepared and submitted in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics Magazine has a double-anonymous review policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should prepare manuscripts consistent with double-anonymous review (i.e., anonymize identifying information) and consult the magazine's refereeing guide/templates for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of LaTeX templates and style files
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must download and use the LaTeX Style File with the article, note, and filler templates before uploading submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the provided LaTeX templates and style files exactly when preparing submissions to ensure correct formatting and to facilitate review and production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem proposals must be accompanied by solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted problems should include complete solutions and must not be under consideration for publication elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / simultaneous submission prohibition (for problems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted problems should not be under consideration for publication elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure originality of submission and avoid simultaneous submissions; include full solutions with problem proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refereeing resources and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Refereeing for the Mathematics Magazine is supported by a Guide for Referees and Referee Templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees (and authors wishing to understand evaluation criteria) should consult the guide and templates to learn the magazine's evaluation standards and recommended review format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprint permission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: General permission is granted to institutional members of the MAA for noncommercial reproduction in limited quantities of individual articles (in whole or in part) provided a complete reference is made to the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reprint permission beyond this, or for other reproduction requests, contact Taylor and Francis using the provided reprint request form or email addresses.
